transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because... well, I work in retail, and lately I just can't make myself go near the front windows. Or even that part of the street, honestly. I keep finding excuses to stay in the back room, even though working the floor is my actual job. It's just getting really hard to manage.
Did something traumatic happen near those front windows or on that part of the street?
Yeah. Um, this has been going on for about two weeks now. It started ever since a car crashed right through the store window while I was working an overnight shift.
Since the crash, have you been having unwanted memories of it that pop into your mind?

Yeah, I have. The crash just keeps popping into my head out of nowhere. It happens a lot, especially when I’m trying to set up displays. It's like... suddenly I can hear the bang again, and I see all the glass coming down just like it’s happening all over again.
When you’re near the front windows or that part of the street, does your body suddenly react with things like your heart pounding or feeling shaky?

No, not really. I mean, I definitely feel anxious and I just want to get away from there, but my heart doesn't start pounding or anything like that. I don't get shaky. I just... I just avoid it as much as I can.
Have you been having nightmares about the crash?
No, I haven't really had any nightmares about it. I mean, my sleep hasn't been great, but I don't wake up from bad dreams about the crash or anything like that.
How long has it been since the car crashed through the store window?
It's been about two weeks. Yeah, it happened during my overnight shift, so... it's been going on for two weeks since then.
Since the crash, have you been feeling constantly on guard or watchful, like you’re scanning for danger?

No, not really. I mean, I don't think I'm constantly on guard or looking out for danger all the time. I just try to stay away from the front of the store, but I'm not, like, scanning the room or jumping at every little thing.
When those memories hit, does it ever feel like the crash is happening again right then, as if you’re back there in that moment?

Yeah, it actually does. The crash just keeps popping into my head out of nowhere. Like, especially when I'm trying to set up displays or something, suddenly it's like I can hear that huge bang again. And I can actually see the glass coming down, just like it's happening all over again right in front of me.
Since the crash, have you found that you can’t remember an important part of what happened during it?
No, I remember everything. I haven't forgotten any part of it, honestly. I kind of wish I could, but... yeah, the whole thing is still pretty clear in my head.
Since the crash, have you had upsetting dreams about what happened?

No, I haven't really had any bad dreams about it. I mean, I'm definitely having trouble sleeping since it happened, but when I do sleep, I don't remember dreaming about the crash or anything like that.
When those memories hit, do you lose awareness of what’s going on around you?

Not really. I mean, even when the memory is super clear and I can hear the bang and everything, I still know I'm at work or wherever I am. I don't totally blank out or forget where I am, it's just... the memory is really intense. But I'm still aware of my surroundings.
Since the crash, have you been feeling unable to experience positive emotions, like happiness or closeness?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I'm obviously pretty stressed out right now, but I can still feel happy. Like, when I'm with my friends or my family, I still feel close to them and we still joke around and stuff. I haven't lost that or gone completely numb or anything.
Since the crash, have you been getting easily startled by sudden noises or movements?

Yes, definitely. It happens a lot, especially at work. If a delivery cart bangs in the back room, or... or even if a car just honks outside, I jump so hard my whole body jerks. And if someone walks up behind me and I didn't hear them coming, it's the same thing. My heart just starts pounding, and it keeps racing for a good while afterward. I'm just really jumpy right now.
Have these symptoms continued for more than one month since the crash?

No, it hasn't been a month yet. It's been about two weeks. This all started right after that overnight shift when the car crashed through the front window of the store. So, yeah, just about two weeks of dealing with this.
Since the crash, have there been moments when you felt detached from yourself, like you were watching yourself from the outside?

Yeah, actually, I have. It's a really weird feeling. Sometimes when I'm out on the sales floor, the lights and the clothing racks just start to feel... I don't know, kind of far away and fake. It's almost exactly like you said, like I'm just watching myself move through the store instead of really being there in my own body.
When that happens on the sales floor, does the store ever feel unreal or dreamlike to you?

Yeah, exactly. That's kind of what I meant when I said it feels fake. It really does feel like a dream, or just... not real. Like I was saying, everything just seems so far away, and I'm just going through the motions of walking around the store instead of actually being there. It's a really strange feeling.
